reviews.summary: Read-only review of the F03 D1 consumer scan (authorization.server.ts consumerOf / classifyDeviceWrite) and promotion re-classification (manager.server.ts promoteStaged). One real defect found: the read-only-tool exemption is applied per simple command by substring match, so a runner that consumes *.md is missed when a read-only tool word appears elsewhere in that command or the glob sits in a read-only segment of a pipeline. The promotion re-classification uses the same classifier, so it does not catch this. Impact is bounded by owner promotion review and the Host-wide code-run review gate. The uncommitted F04 hunks in bunny-missions/manager.server.ts (liveCodeExecutions adds liveHostCodeRuns) and bunny-host/manager.server.ts (restart provider-session reconciliation and holds) only add live-code gating; I did not find a weakening of F01-F03 in them, though I only skimmed them. No tests were run and no files were changed.

rows.title: Read-only tool exemption is substring-matched per command, so a runner consuming *.md is classified as a plain document
rows.scenario: The project has a root-level shell or Makefile consumer (automatic scan, SHELL_RUN) containing either `node render.js *.md   # grep` or `node render.js $(ls *.md)`, or a pipeline `ls *.md | xargs -n1 node render.js`. A paired device writes `notes.md` at the project root with ordinary Markdown prose. In consumerOf, extensionGlob matches `*.md`, but READ_ONLY_TOOL (a \b-bounded regex on the whole simple command) matches the word `ls`/`grep` inside the comment or the substitution, so the command is exempt. In the pipeline case the glob sits in the `ls *.md` segment, which is exempt, and the `xargs node render.js` segment has no glob. Result: no consumer is found and classifyDeviceWrite returns PHONE_SAFE_DOCUMENT, even though the render tool receives every root .md file by default. promoteStaged re-runs the same classifier on the exact staged bytes (manager.server.ts ~line 2655), gets the same PHONE_SAFE_DOCUMENT, and enforces it only for remote envelopes, so promotion does not catch it. Mitigations that limit impact: the workstation must still approve the promotion request, and Bunny code runs are gated on Host review of paired-device content. Neither mitigation sees the misclassification, because the approval prompt shows the stored staging-time class.
rows.evidence: authorization.server.ts:597 READ_ONLY_TOOL = /\b(prettier|...|grep|rg|ls)\b/ is tested against each `commands` element, which is `run.split(/\n|&&|\|\||;|\||&/)` (line ~695). The exemption is `shell ? !READ_ONLY_TOOL.test(command)` (line ~699). A `$(ls *.md)` argument or a trailing `# grep` comment is inside the same command string, and comments are stripped only for full lines (shellLines). The pipe split at `|` leaves the glob only in the read-only segment. The shell computed-glob fail-closed regex (line ~689) requires `$(...)` immediately followed by `/?*`, so it does not match `$(ls *.md)`. The existing test F03-R2-5/F03-R3-1 covers only `prettier --write **/*.md` and `markdownlint ... && mdsh **/*.md`, not substitution, trailing comments or pipes. manager.server.ts promoteStaged: `reclassified` is computed from the same classifyDeviceWrite, and it is only enforced for `staged.envelopeRemote && !PHONE_SAFE_CLASSES.includes(...)` and for UNKNOWN.

votes.reasoning:
Verified by static reading only (no tests run, no files changed). The claim holds.

1. authorization.server.ts:597 defines READ_ONLY_TOOL as a \b-bounded regex over the whole simple command. Line ~695 splits the run text into commands on \n, &&, ||, ;, |, &. Line ~699 exempts a shell command when `!READ_ONLY_TOOL.test(command)` fails, so any read-only word anywhere in that command string exempts it.

2. Trailing comment: shellLines (line ~553) drops only full lines starting with #. A Makefile line `\tnode render.js *.md   # grep` keeps the `# grep` text. The command contains `*.md`, which matches extensionGlob, and `grep`, which matches READ_ONLY_TOOL. It is exempt, and the bareGlob path does not fire because the glob is not bare `*`.

3. Substitution: `node render.js $(ls *.md)`. The computed-glob fail-closed regex (line ~689) requires `$(...)` immediately followed by `/?*`, so it does not match. The command contains `ls`, so it is exempt.

4. Pipeline: `ls *.md | xargs -n1 node render.js`. The split on `|` leaves the glob only in the `ls *.md` segment, which is exempt. The `xargs node render.js` segment has no extension glob, so nothing fires.

5. Promotion does not catch it. manager.server.ts:2676 re-runs the same classifyDeviceWrite on the exact staged bytes. Line 2678 enforces only when staged.envelopeRemote and the class is outside PHONE_SAFE_CLASSES. A PHONE_SAFE_DOCUMENT result passes.

6. Existing tests (f03-hardening.test.ts F03-R2-5, F03-R3-1) cover only `mdsh **/*.md`, `markdownlint ... && mdsh **/*.md`, `ls && sh **/*.md` (which is refused only because the glob is after the read-only segment), and `prettier --write **/*.md`. None cover substitution, trailing comments or pipelines.

Refutation attempts that do not succeed: the classifier is not short-circuited earlier for a root .md (the Makefile is a non-document root file, so it is scanned by check()). The mitigations (inert staging, Host-owner review of exact bytes, Bunny code runs gated on Host review) reduce impact, but the approval prompt displays the stored PHONE_SAFE_DOCUMENT class, so the reviewer is not told a runner consumes the file. That is a real gap in the F03 R2-5/R3-1 exemption contract. I did not review the uncommitted F04 diff in this pass.

Verified by reading the code (no edits, tests or git state changes).

Confirmed:
- authorization.server.ts:597 READ_ONLY_TOOL is an unanchored \b-bounded regex tested against each simple command. Line ~699 uses `shell ? !READ_ONLY_TOOL.test(command)`, so any read-only word anywhere in the command exempts it.
- The root Makefile is scanned. SHELL_RUN (line 549) matches extensionless names via `[^.]*$`. The root loop (around line 727) skips only OPAQUE, DATA, and DOCUMENT files, so Makefile reaches check() with shell=true.
- `node render.js $(ls *.md)`: the fail-closed regex at line ~689 requires `$(...)` followed by `/?*`, so it does not fire. extensionGlob matches `*.md)`, and READ_ONLY_TOOL matches `ls` inside the substitution, so the line is exempt.
- `node render.js *.md   # grep`: shellLines drops only full-line comments, so `grep` in the trailing comment exempts the line, while make and sh still expand the glob.
- `ls *.md | xargs -n1 node render.js`: the split at `|` leaves the glob only in the exempt `ls` segment, and the xargs segment has no glob. Pipe-split commands are judged separately, so no consumer is found.
- For a root-level notes.md, the folder-ref and tokenIn checks cannot match, so the only path to a consumer is the glob check, and it is bypassed. classifyDeviceWrite then reaches the DOCUMENT_FILE branch and returns PHONE_SAFE_DOCUMENT.
- manager.server.ts:2676-2678: promoteStaged re-runs the same classifier on the staged bytes, and enforces the class only when staged.envelopeRemote is true. The re-run returns the same wrong class, so it passes.

Limits of the finding: the defect is real, but impact is bounded. The consumer must already exist in the project, the render step runs only when someone runs make, and promotion still needs workstation approval. That approval prompt shows the generic "plain document" reason and does not show the consumer list. I did not verify the claimed Host-review gate on Bunny code runs. I did not review the uncommitted F04 changes, which were outside this finding's scope.

Suggested fix direction: make the read-only exemption apply per glob-bearing simple command, after stripping trailing # comments and $(...) substitutions, and only when the read-only tool is the command's program word. Alternatively, fail closed whenever a shell consumer contains an extension glob together with any substitution or pipe.

reviews.summary: Read-only independent follow-up review of F03 final-round fixes (commit b693167) and the uncommitted F04 working tree. No real defects survived verification, so findings is empty. Two candidate defects I found in the F04 restart-hold code (folder-level unreadable release without reconciling records, and readProviderSessions rewriting this Host's live job records because currentGeneration was null) are already fixed in the current working tree: manager.server.ts now passes this.instanceId, and the FOLDER_UNREADABLE release path reconciles every record and re-holds still-unreadable files. Checked and found sound: promotion reads and hash-verifies the staged bytes once (readVerified), re-classifies those same bytes, and writes those same bytes, so there is no TOCTOU between classify and write; Retry's refusal checks (state, ceiling, envelope) all run before revokeDesktopGrants, withdrawStaged or setStep, and the abandoned running attempt is closed; Replan's one-time withdrawal goes through stampLifecycle("WITHDRAWN") and keeps completed steps; liveCodeExecutions only adds gates (liveHostCodeRuns, restart survivors, unreadable holds), so F01 device-no-execute and F02 inert staging/promotion are not weakened. Not verified: tests were not run, and the working tree was changing during the review.
